title: Governed Launch Chorus and Capacity Sentry
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Objective: build a governed, observable launch calendar feature set that coordinates runtime/console/API release trains and automatically reserves surge capacity lanes ("Capacity Sentry") for high-risk launches. Scope: produce a cross-team cadence playbook, console signals (launch health, capacity headroom), a release-train gating API, and an automated capacity hedge that can be exercised by PMs during cutover windows. Goals: 1) reduce unexpected throttling for high-traffic launches by 60% in first month post-launch; 2) provide a single source of truth launch calendar with per-release SLA/latency guardrails; 3) enable safe canary expansion across regions via automated cohort signals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook published and reviewed by Eng/Design/SRE; 2) Console dashboard shows launch lanes + capacity headroom with <5s query latency; 3) Release-train gating API accepted by runtime and console teams and supports canary cohort configuration; 4) Capacity Sentry can reserve and release burst capacity via Dedicated autoscale policy with audit logs; 5) Runbook for rollback and surge unwinding validated in a shadow rehearsal.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): align on schema for launch objects, SLA fields, and surge profile; build minimal console signals and a mock gating API. Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement Capacity Sentry integration with Dedicated autoscale and P0/P1 policies; wire dashboards and alerts. Phase 3 (2 weeks): cross-team rehearsal (shadow traffic) and adjust policies; final sign-off. Post-launch (1 month): telemetry evaluation and feedback loop to Optimize team.
metrics: Primary: % launches with throttling incidents, mean time to scale for surge lanes, per-token latency p95 during launch windows. Secondary: time-to-declare-surge (minutes), false-positive surge activations.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-reserving capacity and increasing cost. Mitigation: conservative default surge thresholds + cost-budget guardrail in console. Risk: inconsistent metadata across teams. Mitigation: canonical launch schema and lightweight validation in gating API. Risk: rollout causes cascading autoscale churn. Mitigation: rate-limited surge release and circuit-breaker thresholds.
